[`Bot`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/bot.html#bot) combines
[`DiscordClient`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#discordclient)
(REST) and
[`GatewayClient`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/gateway.html#gatewayclient)
(events) with a command router. `@bot.cmd` registers a handler under the
function’s name. `def echo` answers `!echo`. A handler takes the
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/core.html#message)
and a string holding everything after the command name, empty if
nothing.

`_on_msg` ignores messages from the bot itself. Without that, a bot that
answers its own messages loops forever. It splits the message into
command name and args: `!echo hello world` passes `"hello world"` as
`args`.

### Bot

``` python
def Bot(
    intents, **kw
):
```

*Discord bot with command routing*

``` python
bot = Bot(intents)
await bot.start()
```

You can register commands after `bot.start()`. `@bot.cmd` adds the
function to a dict, and the message handler looks commands up on each
message.

``` python
@bot.cmd
async def echo(msg, args): await (await msg.channel()).send(f'You said: {args}')
```

``` python
bot
```

    Bot(cmds=['echo'])

The router catches errors in command handlers and appends them to
`bot.errors`. You can inspect that list after the fact, for example in
solveit. `@bot.on_error` registers a handler for real-time handling,
such as notifying the user in Discord. Both work at the same time.

### Bot.on_error

``` python
def on_error(
    f
):
```

``` python
@bot.on_error
async def handle_err(msg, e): print('error')
```

``` python
@bot.cmd
def err(msg): raise Exception('test')
```

Voice reuses
[`VoiceClient`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/voice.html#voiceclient).
[`Bot`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/cordslite/bot.html#bot) adds
`join_voice` and `leave_voice` to manage its lifecycle. A bot can be in
one voice channel at a time.
